To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the processing of music syntax and semantics involves similar neural substrates and processes as those involved in language processing.
music-syntatic processing can be observed in the brain at about 150-400 ms after the onset of a music event and that musical semantics are processed at about 300-500 ms.
music syntax and semantics are processed in different brain regions and that these regions overlap considerably with the brain regions that process syntax and semantics of language.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of what neural mechanisms underlie the perception of music.
the neurocognitive processes underlying music and language, in particular with syntax and semantics, which are the basic aspects in music and language.
the neurocognitive mechanisms underlying the processing of musical syntax and semantics, with an emphasis on the similarities and differences to language processing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
music is processed in a similar fashion as language.
the processing of music syntax is similar to the processing of linguistic syntax and the processing of musical semantics is similar to the process of linguistic semantics.

musical syntax and semantics are processed in a manner similar to the processing of language syntax and semantics, respectively, and that the neural mechanisms of music and language processing are closely interrelated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the processing of musical syntax and semantics is a dynamic process in which the brain structures involved in processing syntax and semantics are activated in an interactive and dynamic fashion.
musical syntax and semantics are processed in the brain in a similar manner as syntax and semantics in language.
music and language are closely related in terms of both their processing and their neural substrates.
The main takeaway from our work is that
musical syntax and semantics are processed in a manner that is similar to language syntax and semantics.
the neural substrates of music perception and production are not specific to the processing of music, but rather are shared with other domains, such as language and action.
